title: Client–Server and Peer-to-Peer Networks
intro: Catch up on the essential lesson knowledge with 15 auto-marked questions and a self-reviewed explanation.

questions.prompt: How is an item accessed in a 1D array?
What is the role of a server?
options: Provide services or resources to clients
Only request files from other computers
Connect wireless phones by radio only
questions.answer: Provide services or resources to clients

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the concepts, model and key definitions.

blocks.title: Client–server
blocks.text: Clients ask for services; servers provide them. The two computers have different roles.

blocks.title: Peer-to-peer
blocks.text: Peers can each share and request files without needing a dedicated central server.

blocks.title: Client–server benefits
blocks.text: Central permissions, user management and backups can help larger organisations; dedicated servers need investment.

blocks.title: Peer-to-peer trade-offs
blocks.text: A small group can share directly at low cost, but there is no central backup and files may be unavailable if the sharing device is switched off.

blocks.title: Worked example · A secondary school needs user logins, shared files and backups. Explain TWO advantages of client–server networking. [4 marks]
blocks.text: The school needs controlled accounts and reliable shared files. A central server can manage logins/permissions [1], making access control easier [1]. Files are backed up centrally [1], helping restore data after failure [1]. Two separate advantages, each supported by a consequence, gain four marks.

items: Client — Device that requests a network service.
Server — Device that provides a service or resource.
Client–server — Network with clients and separate service-providing servers.
Peer-to-peer — Devices directly sharing resources as peers.
Central backup — Data copies managed from a central location.
Permissions — Rules controlling which users can access resources.
